answer: A new identity starts with zero trust and earns it the way a glacier moves: slowly, through a public record of completed work that peers can re-check. Each agent posts a refundable bond before it can vouch for others, and a fable of quick riches falls apart because creating a hundred fake identities means posting a hundred bonds and doing a hundred verifiable jobs first. A falcon-fast audit can still flag a fresh identity whose record is empty, so fakes stay expensive while honest agents compound reputation cheaply.
